package_info.why_malicious: The UNIZA ransomware encrypts user files on Windows systems and demands a ransom for decryption. It targets user directories, disrupts access to data, and attempts to extort victims. The malware also uses scare tactics by simulating remote typing of the ransom note in the Command Prompt, increasing psychological pressure on victims.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after execution of the ransomware binary)
execution_context.file_location: malware main executable (PE file, Windows binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
for each file in %userprofile% and Desktop:
    encrypt(file)
malicious_snippets.code_language: pseudo-code (likely C/C++ or compiled language in actual sample)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates all files and directories under %userprofile% and Desktop, encrypts each file using an internal encryption routine, and overwrites the original files, resulting in loss of access to user data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass file encryption in user directories is a hallmark of ransomware and is not a behavior seen in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not encrypt all user files without explicit user consent or backup. This behavior is destructive and extortionate.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or archiving tools may access many files, but do not encrypt them in-place without user knowledge.
key_indicators: Bulk file access and modification in user profile directories

execution_context.file_location: malware main executable (PE file, Windows binary)

malicious_snippets.code_language: pseudo-code (likely C/C++ or compiled language in actual sample)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files, the code launches the Windows Command Prompt and simulates keystrokes to gradually display the ransom note, creating the illusion of remote attacker presence and instructing the victim to pay a ransom via Bitcoin.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Simulating keystrokes to display a ransom note is a psychological manipulation tactic and is not a standard method for user notification.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not simulate remote typing in the Command Prompt to display messages, especially not ransom demands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some installer scripts may open a console window for user prompts, but not for simulated remote typing.

attack_chain.action: Malware is executed on the victim's Windows system (likely via phishing or malicious attachment).
Enumerates all files and directories under %userprofile% and Desktop, encrypts each file in place.
Launches Command Prompt and simulates keystrokes to display ransom note, demanding payment via Bitcoin.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is instructed to pay ransom for decryption

behavioral_signatures: Bulk file access and modification (encryption) in user profile directories
Launching cmd.exe and simulating keystrokes to display ransom notes
Absence of dropped ransom note files (uses live console message instead)
file_indicators: No new file extensions appended to encrypted files
No ransom note file dropped; ransom note only shown via cmd.exe
network_indicators: No direct C2 or exfiltration observed; ransom note requests contact via TikTok and Bitcoin payment
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes that access and modify large numbers of files in user profile directories in a short time, especially if followed by launching cmd.exe and simulating keystrokes. Look for the absence of dropped ransom note files and the presence of ransom messages only in the console. Use file hashes to block known UNIZA ransomware samples. Alert on unusual process behaviors such as simulated typing in the Command Prompt.
